findings.title: Modal eigen-analysis repeated on every trial step
findings.message: Two full modal analyses run on every trial step that passes the error test. Each analysis does count+1 dense MNA solves, an eigendecomposition and count complex solves. When the modal check is what rejects the step, the step is halved and both analyses run again. This happens before the hybrid-guard check, so their results can also be thrown away. On networks near the work guard, this can use up the integration budget, which matches the documented 'may still reach the work guard' limitation.
findings.suggestion: Cache the midpoint and endpoint analyses per step size, or skip them when h is already well below the current ceiling, e.g. `if h < 0.25*ceiling` keep the ceiling. Alternatively, run them only once a step is otherwise ready to be accepted.

findings.title: mnaEquations failure ignored before mutating rows
findings.message: The second return value of mnaEquations is discarded. If it reports a failure, `base` may be nil or partial. The code then indexes `base[row]`, which can panic or build a Jacobian from invalid equations. Because the rows are also overwritten in place, any matrix the network keeps internally could be corrupted.
findings.suggestion: Check the second result and return `nil, false` on failure. Also verify that `len(base)` covers every capacitor and inductor index before indexing. Copy the matrix if mnaEquations might return a cached slice.
findings.evidence: base, _ := n.mnaEquations(state.x, nil, 1, trace, at, false)

findings.title: Discrete graph built then discarded for speaker example
findings.message: For class-ab-speaker, the code first builds DiscreteClassABExampleGraph and sets its probes, then throws both away. This wastes work, and folding two examples into one case makes the configuration harder to follow.
findings.suggestion: Give class-ab-speaker its own `case` that builds only ClassABSpeakerExampleGraph and sets its own settings.

findings.title: Deadline test may not exercise modal probing path
findings.message: The test says it checks that modal probing respects the deadline. However, the clock is already past `MaxIntegrationWallTime` before `advanceBudget` starts. The step will likely be refused at the first deadline check, before any modal analysis runs. If modal probing ignored the deadline, this test would still pass.
findings.suggestion: Use a clock that advances on each call, or one that expires only after `budget.modalAnalyses > 0`. Then assert `modalAnalyses >= 1` and that the step was still refused, so the test exercises a deadline hit during or after modal probing.
findings.evidence: budget.elapsed = func() time.Duration { return MaxIntegrationWallTime + time.Nanosecond }

findings.title: Removed discrete Class AB production-clock coverage
findings.message: The removed test built an all-discrete Class AB circuit with a substituted speaker and checked conservation over 10 real-clock steps. Its replacement only checks behaviour when the deadline has already expired. If `ClassABSpeakerExampleGraph` differs from the substituted `DiscreteClassABExampleGraph`, the original circuit no longer has budget coverage under the production clock.
findings.suggestion: Confirm that `ClassABSpeakerExampleGraph` covers the old circuit. If it does not, keep a production-clock smoke test for the discrete Class AB plus speaker case.

findings.title: Atomicity test ignores storage and proposal fields
findings.message: The atomicity test only compares the serialized `result`. It does not check that `state.x`, `state.capV`, `inductorStep` or `inductorCeiling` are unchanged after the refused step. These are the private fields this change adds, and a refused step could mutate them in place without the test noticing.
findings.suggestion: Before calling `advanceBudget`, snapshot `state.x`, `state.capV`, `state.inductorStep` and `state.inductorCeiling`. After the call, assert each is unchanged, as `TestModalLegacyFallbackDeadlineAndOldNetworkPreservation` does.

finding.title: Exact float equality on accumulated simulation time
finding.message: The parity test compares the simulated time to `.0001` with exact equality. The step is integrated adaptively and the time is built by summing sub-intervals. Accumulated floating-point rounding (e.g. 0.0001 as a sum of halves or quarters plus a remainder) can produce a value a few ULPs away. That makes the test brittle, or causes it to fail on harmless solver changes.
finding.suggestion: Compare with a tolerance, e.g. `math.Abs(a.Mixed.Time-.0001) > 1e-12`, and add the `math` import.
